items.title: Understanding the Different Gearbox Types
items.description: Different vehicle transmissions utilize radically different engineering architectures, impacting parts availability, rebuilding complexity, and labour time.

cards.title: Manual
cards.text: Traditional transmission with clutch pedal and gear lever. Highly durable, simpler internal architecture, lowest rebuilding and repair costs.
cards.highlight: Typical cost: £800–£4,500 fitted | Most cars up to 2015
cards.fullText: ⚙️ Manual Traditional transmission with clutch pedal and gear lever. Highly durable, simpler internal architecture, lowest rebuilding and repair costs. Typical cost: £800–£4,500 fitted | Most cars up to 2015

cards.title: Automatic (Traditional)
cards.text: Torque-converter automatic with planetary gear sets and hydraulic valve body. Proven long-term reliability but requires specialist rebuilding benches.
cards.highlight: Typical cost: £1,500–£6,500+ fitted | BMW, Mercedes, Lexus
cards.fullText: 🕹️ Automatic (Traditional) Torque-converter automatic with planetary gear sets and hydraulic valve body. Proven long-term reliability but requires specialist rebuilding benches. Typical cost: £1,500–£6,500+ fitted | BMW, Mercedes, Lexus

cards.title: DSG / DCT
cards.text: Dual-clutch transmission providing lightning-quick shifts. Complex mechatronic control units and wet/dry clutch assemblies drive higher replacement costs.
cards.highlight: Typical cost: £2,000–£7,500+ fitted | VW Group, Porsche, BMW M
cards.fullText: ⚡ DSG / DCT Dual-clutch transmission providing lightning-quick shifts. Complex mechatronic control units and wet/dry clutch assemblies drive higher replacement costs. Typical cost: £2,000–£7,500+ fitted | VW Group, Porsche, BMW M

cards.title: CVT
cards.text: Continuously variable transmission with steel belt and conical pulleys. Smooth stepless acceleration; high repair costs due to limited rebuild component supply.
cards.highlight: Typical cost: £2,000–£6,500+ fitted | Nissan, Honda, Toyota
cards.fullText: 🔄 CVT Continuously variable transmission with steel belt and conical pulleys. Smooth stepless acceleration; high repair costs due to limited rebuild component supply. Typical cost: £2,000–£6,500+ fitted | Nissan, Honda, Toyota

cards.title: Semi-Automatic
cards.text: Automated manual with robotic clutch pedal actuators. Common in older city cars; actuator motor failures often misdiagnosed as mechanical gearbox failure.
cards.highlight: Typical cost: £1,000–£3,500 fitted | Renault, Peugeot, Citroën
cards.fullText: 🎛️ Semi-Automatic Automated manual with robotic clutch pedal actuators. Common in older city cars; actuator motor failures often misdiagnosed as mechanical gearbox failure. Typical cost: £1,000–£3,500 fitted | Renault, Peugeot, Citroën

cards.title: Transfer Box (4WD)
cards.text: Distributes power between front and rear axles. Requires dedicated removal and overhaul separate from main transmission casing.
cards.highlight: Typical cost: £800–£3,000 fitted | Range Rover, Audi quattro, BMW xDrive
cards.fullText: 🚙 Transfer Box (4WD) Distributes power between front and rear axles. Requires dedicated removal and overhaul separate from main transmission casing. Typical cost: £800–£3,000 fitted | Range Rover, Audi quattro, BMW xDrive

blocks.text: Why DSG/DCT and CVT cost more: DSG/DCT units have two clutches and complex mechatronics. CVTs require specialized knowledge and expensive steel belts. Traditional automatics are more common and most specialists can work on them easily.

items.title: What does gearbox replacement cost in the UK?
items.description: The short answer: Gearbox replacement costs range from £500 to £6,500+ depending on gearbox type and condition. Manual gearboxes cost £500–£3,000 , while automatic transmissions range from £1,000–£5,000 . DSG/DCT and CVT gearboxes typically cost £2,000–£6,500+ .

items.title: How to Spot a Failing Gearbox
items.description: Catching gearbox issues early can save you thousands — a simpler component repair may cost £200–£500, while a full catastrophic replacement could cost £1,000–£5,000+.

cards.title: Slipping (auto)
cards.text: Engine revs up but car doesn't accelerate properly - worn clutches, low fluid.
cards.fullText: ⚠️ Slipping (auto) Engine revs up but car doesn't accelerate properly - worn clutches, low fluid.

cards.title: Grinding (manual)
cards.text: Noise when changing gear - worn synchronisers, damaged gears.
cards.fullText: 🔊 Grinding (manual) Noise when changing gear - worn synchronisers, damaged gears.

cards.title: Delayed engagement
cards.text: Delay when selecting drive/reverse - low fluid, worn valve body.
cards.fullText: ⏳ Delayed engagement Delay when selecting drive/reverse - low fluid, worn valve body.

cards.title: Whining / Moaning
cards.text: Noise in neutral or when driving - worn bearings, low fluid.
cards.fullText: 📢 Whining / Moaning Noise in neutral or when driving - worn bearings, low fluid.

cards.title: Clunking
cards.text: Noise when changing gear or engaging drive - worn mounts, damaged internals.
cards.fullText: 💥 Clunking Noise when changing gear or engaging drive - worn mounts, damaged internals.

cards.title: Leaking fluid
cards.text: Red/brown fluid under the car - worn seals, cracked casing.
cards.fullText: 💧 Leaking fluid Red/brown fluid under the car - worn seals, cracked casing.

cards.title: Warning lights
cards.text: Gearbox warning light on dashboard - electronic issue, low fluid.
cards.fullText: 🚨 Warning lights Gearbox warning light on dashboard - electronic issue, low fluid.

cards.title: Jarring shifts (auto/DSG)
cards.text: Harsh or jerky gear changes - worn valve body, low fluid, software issue.
cards.fullText: ⚡ Jarring shifts (auto/DSG) Harsh or jerky gear changes - worn valve body, low fluid, software issue.

blocks.text: What to do if you notice symptoms: Check fluid level and for leaks. Have it inspected by a specialist. Don't ignore symptoms — they won't get better. A diagnostic check can identify issues before they become catastrophic.

blocks.text: DSG/DCT specific considerations: Mechatronic (control unit) often fails and is expensive to replace (£1,000-£2,500). Clutch packs wear out (£1,000-£2,000). Only certain transmission specialists work on DSG/DCT. VAG-COM / VCDS or equivalent required for proper diagnosis.

cards.title: Question 1
cards.text: Get a full written breakdown. Ask about: gearbox supply, fitting, fluid, clutch (manual), torque converter (auto), mechatronic, and testing.
cards.fullText: Question 1 "What's included in the price." Get a full written breakdown. Ask about: gearbox supply, fitting, fluid, clutch (manual), torque converter (auto), mechatronic, and testing.

cards.title: Question 2
cards.text: Ask about: warranty length, parts vs parts and labour, exclusions, mileage limit, and how to claim.
cards.fullText: Question 2 "What warranty do you offer and what does it cover." Ask about: warranty length, parts vs parts and labour, exclusions, mileage limit, and how to claim.

cards.title: Question 3
cards.text: If replacing a manual gearbox, ask if the clutch and DMF are included. It's recommended to replace these while the gearbox is out.
cards.fullText: Question 3 "Is the clutch/DMF included (manual)." If replacing a manual gearbox, ask if the clutch and DMF are included. It's recommended to replace these while the gearbox is out.

cards.title: Question 4
cards.text: For automatic gearboxes, ask if the torque converter is included. Many recon units exclude this.
cards.fullText: Question 4 "Is the torque converter included (auto)." For automatic gearboxes, ask if the torque converter is included. Many recon units exclude this.

cards.title: Question 5
cards.text: For automatic and DSG gearboxes, ask if the control unit is included. This is often a significant extra cost.
cards.fullText: Question 5 "Is the mechatronic/control unit included (auto/DSG)." For automatic and DSG gearboxes, ask if the control unit is included. This is often a significant extra cost.

cards.title: Question 6
cards.text: Gearbox fluid is expensive and must be the correct spec. Ask if it's included and what brand/type is used.
cards.fullText: Question 6 "What fluid is used and who supplies it." Gearbox fluid is expensive and must be the correct spec. Ask if it's included and what brand/type is used.

cards.title: Question 7
cards.text: Get a realistic estimate. Manual FWD fitting typically takes 1-2 days; auto/DSG 4WD takes 2-4 days.
cards.fullText: Question 7 "What's the timeline for replacement." Get a realistic estimate. Manual FWD fitting typically takes 1-2 days; auto/DSG 4WD takes 2-4 days.

cards.title: Question 8
cards.text: Some gearboxes require specialist knowledge and tools. Ask about their experience with your specific gearbox.
cards.fullText: Question 8 "Do you have experience with my gearbox type." Some gearboxes require specialist knowledge and tools. Ask about their experience with your specific gearbox.

cards.title: Question 9
cards.text: Get everything in writing before agreeing. The scope of work, cost, timeline, and warranty terms should all be documented.
cards.fullText: Question 9 "Can you provide a written quote." Get everything in writing before agreeing. The scope of work, cost, timeline, and warranty terms should all be documented.

cards.title: Question 10
cards.text: During fitting, other issues may be discovered (worn mounts, drive shafts, etc.). Ask how these are handled.
cards.fullText: Question 10 "What happens if additional issues are discovered." During fitting, other issues may be discovered (worn mounts, drive shafts, etc.). Ask how these are handled.

items.title: Common Questions About Gearbox Replacement
items.description: Find answers to the most common queries regarding gearbox repairs, replacements, costs, and diagnostics in the UK.

blocks.question: How much does gearbox replacement cost in the UK? +
blocks.answer: Gearbox replacement costs range from £500 to £6,500+ depending on gearbox type and condition. Manual gearboxes cost £500–£3,000, while automatic transmissions range from £1,000–£5,000. DSG/DCT and CVT gearboxes typically cost £2,000–£6,500+. Most owners pay between £1,500 and £4,000 fitted.

blocks.question: What's the difference between reconditioned and used gearboxes? +
blocks.answer: A used gearbox is removed from a donor vehicle and sold as-is with basic testing. A reconditioned gearbox is completely dismantled, cleaned, inspected, and rebuilt with new wear components (bearings, seals, synchros, clutch packs) and tested to OEM tolerances. Reconditioned units come with longer warranties (6-12 months vs 1-3 months for used).

blocks.question: Should I replace the clutch when replacing a manual gearbox? +
blocks.answer: Yes, absolutely. The gearbox must be removed to access the clutch, so there is zero additional labour cost to replace the clutch at the same time. You only pay for parts (£100-£300 for clutch kit, £400-£1,000 if dual-mass flywheel is needed). If you don't replace an aged clutch, you risk paying 4-8 hours of labour (£300-£800) again if the clutch fails shortly after.

blocks.question: How long does gearbox replacement take? +
blocks.answer: Labour time typically ranges from 5 to 15 hours depending on drivetrain layout. Front-wheel drive manual vehicles take 5-8 hours. Rear-wheel drive vehicles take 6-10 hours. All-wheel drive and 4WD vehicles take 8-15 hours. Total turnaround at a garage is usually 2 to 4 working days, or longer if a unit needs to be custom reconditioned.

blocks.question: What's the labour rate for gearbox replacement? +
blocks.answer: Independent transmission specialists charge between £60 and £95 per hour (+VAT). Independent general garages charge £55 to £85/hr. Franchised main dealers charge £110 to £220+/hr. We strongly recommend using dedicated transmission specialists for complex automatic, DSG, and CVT repairs.

blocks.question: Should I use an independent specialist or a main dealer? +
blocks.answer: For out-of-warranty vehicles, independent transmission specialists offer superior value. They possess specialized rebuilding benches and diagnostic tools, charge 40-60% lower labour rates than main dealers, and provide high-quality reconditioned units where dealers typically only sell brand-new OEM assemblies.

blocks.question: What's the most reliable gearbox type? +
blocks.answer: Traditional manual transmissions and torque-converter planetary automatics (such as ZF 6-speed and 8-speed units) have the longest proven track records of longevity when serviced regularly. Dry-clutch DSG/DCT units and push-belt CVTs tend to have higher failure rates and stricter maintenance requirements.

blocks.question: How do I know if my gearbox needs replacing or repairing? +
blocks.answer: Minor issues like external oil leaks, faulty gear linkages, worn solenoid packs, or mechatronic unit faults on DSG boxes can often be repaired in-situ without a full replacement (£200-£1,500). If internal hard parts (gears, shafts, differential, or multiple bearings) have shattered or suffered catastrophic metal contamination, a full reconditioned replacement is more cost-effective.

blocks.question: What's the most common gearbox type in the UK? +
blocks.answer: While manual gearboxes historically dominated the UK car park, automatic transmissions (including torque-converter, DSG/DCT, and CVT) now account for over 60% of new car sales in the UK. On the used market, manuals still represent approximately 50-55% of vehicles on the road.

blocks.question: Do I need to tell my insurer about a replacement gearbox? +
blocks.answer: A standard like-for-like OEM specification gearbox replacement does not need to be declared as a modification, as performance remains standard. However, if you fit a performance uprated gearbox, a different gear ratio set, or convert from manual to automatic, you must declare it to your insurer.

blocks.question: What's the most common gearbox failure? +
blocks.answer: In manual gearboxes: worn synchromesh rings, worn input shaft bearings, and clutch slip. In automatic gearboxes: contaminated/burnt ATF fluid, worn clutch friction plates, and torque converter lock-up failure. In DSG/DCT: mechatronic control unit board failure and clutch pack wear. In CVT: belt/pulley scoring and pump pressure loss.

blocks.question: Should I rebuild or replace my gearbox? +
blocks.answer: If your original gearbox casing is undamaged and specialist parts are available, rebuilding your own unit ensures exact ECU compatibility and original VIN matching. However, an off-the-shelf reconditioned exchange unit is usually faster (saving days of downtime) and comes with pre-certified testing.

blocks.question: What's the difference between DSG and automatic? +
blocks.answer: A traditional automatic uses a hydraulic torque converter and planetary gearsets, providing very smooth, cushioned gear changes. A DSG (Direct-Shift Gearbox) or DCT is an automated dual-clutch manual transmission that pre-selects the next gear for lightning-fast, highly efficient shifts.

blocks.question: How often should I change gearbox fluid? +
blocks.answer: Manual gearboxes should have fluid changed every 60,000-80,000 miles. Traditional automatics every 40,000-60,000 miles. DSG/DCT transmissions require oil and filter service every 40,000 miles (wet-clutch). CVTs require specialized CVT fluid changes every 30,000-40,000 miles. Ignore "sealed for life" claims from manufacturers.

acceptedAnswer.text: Minor issues like external oil leaks, faulty gear linkages, worn solenoid packs, or mechatronic unit faults on DSG boxes can often be repaired in-situ without a full replacement (£200-£1,500). If internal hard parts (gears, shafts, differential, or multiple bearings) have shattered or suffered catastrophic metal contamination, a full reconditioned replacement is more cost-effective.

mainEntity.name: What's the most common gearbox type in the UK?

acceptedAnswer.text: While manual gearboxes historically dominated the UK car park, automatic transmissions (including torque-converter, DSG/DCT, and CVT) now account for over 60% of new car sales in the UK. On the used market, manuals still represent approximately 50-55% of vehicles on the road.

mainEntity.name: Do I need to tell my insurer about a replacement gearbox?

acceptedAnswer.text: A standard like-for-like OEM specification gearbox replacement does not need to be declared as a modification, as performance remains standard. However, if you fit a performance uprated gearbox, a different gear ratio set, or convert from manual to automatic, you must declare it to your insurer.

mainEntity.name: What's the most common gearbox failure?

acceptedAnswer.text: In manual gearboxes: worn synchromesh rings, worn input shaft bearings, and clutch slip. In automatic gearboxes: contaminated/burnt ATF fluid, worn clutch friction plates, and torque converter lock-up failure. In DSG/DCT: mechatronic control unit board failure and clutch pack wear. In CVT: belt/pulley scoring and pump pressure loss.

mainEntity.name: Should I rebuild or replace my gearbox?

acceptedAnswer.text: If your original gearbox casing is undamaged and specialist parts are available, rebuilding your own unit ensures exact ECU compatibility and original VIN matching. However, an off-the-shelf reconditioned exchange unit is usually faster (saving days of downtime) and comes with pre-certified testing.

mainEntity.name: What's the difference between DSG and automatic?

acceptedAnswer.text: A traditional automatic uses a hydraulic torque converter and planetary gearsets, providing very smooth, cushioned gear changes. A DSG (Direct-Shift Gearbox) or DCT is an automated dual-clutch manual transmission that pre-selects the next gear for lightning-fast, highly efficient shifts.

mainEntity.name: How often should I change gearbox fluid?

acceptedAnswer.text: Manual gearboxes should have fluid changed every 60,000-80,000 miles. Traditional automatics every 40,000-60,000 miles. DSG/DCT transmissions require oil and filter service every 40,000 miles (wet-clutch). CVTs require specialized CVT fluid changes every 30,000-40,000 miles. Ignore 'sealed for life' claims from manufacturers.
